title: Rocket Girl's Journey to the West

subtitle.text: It was early morning, and two workers at Shopwell Supermarket were stocking shelves.
"We have too many canned tomatoes, Meg," one worker said, looking in boxes.
"They won't fit on the shelf."
"Let's stack them near the cash registers," Meg said.
"We need to hurry—the store opens soon."
As they carried the boxes down an aisle, Meg spotted some empty shelves.
"We stocked those shelves earlier. Where did all the food go?"
Something crunched under Daryl's foot, and he looked down.
Crumbs and wrappers were scattered across the floor.
"Have you been eating stuff, Daryl?" Meg asked, putting down her box.
"Of course not!" Daryl replied.
"Then who's been eating?"
[i@Snort!@i]
Startled, Daryl dropped his boxes.
"What was that noise?"
Meg gestured toward the end of the aisle, and they tiptoed toward the sound.
[i@Snort!@i] Suddenly a large figure leaped out.
"Ahh!" Meg and Daryl ran.
"Jack, what are you doing?" Miss Apricot asked with a frown.
Jack was crawling on the floor. "My pencil rolled off my desk."
Roxy reached down. "Here it is."
The teacher folded her arms and gave Jack a stern look.
"You're supposed to be reading quietly—not searching for your pencil."
Jack sat down and spun his pencil around.
"My book is boring. I wish it was time for recess."
"I'm enjoying my book," Terrell said.
"It's about the Silk Road."
Mara groaned.
"Is your book boring too?" Roxy asked.
"I like my book, but I'm so hungry," Mara said.
"I can't wait for lunch—it's Pizza Day," Terrell said.
"Mmm, I can smell it cooking," Mara said.
Jack sniffed. "Me too!"
Miss Apricot frowned. "Shh!"
Jack grinned sheepishly. "Sorry!"
Roxy's watch beeped.
"I'll be right back, Miss Apricot.
I need to, um, use the restroom."
Roxy ran into the hallway and opened her watch.
"Mayor Bloom. What's wrong?"
"Rocket Girl," Mayor Bloom said, "there's a food thief in Metro City."
"A food thief?" Roxy repeated.
Mayor Bloom nodded. "The thief is eating food without paying for it."
"I'll check it out, Mayor.
But I usually fight dangerous villains—not somebody who ate a meal and didn't pay."
"The thief didn't just eat a meal," Mayor Bloom said.
"He ate all the food at Shopwell Supermarket!"
"Whoa!" Roxy gasped.
"Then he ate all the food in two other food stores and several restaurants."
Mayor Bloom shook his head. "He's in Metro City Bakery now."
"The thief sounds like some sort of super eater," Roxy said.
"Don't worry, Mayor—I'm on my way!"
When Roxy arrived, police officers had surrounded Metro City Bakery.
Detective Smith was watching from behind a police car.
Roxy floated next to him.
"Hi, Detective—I heard you have a big appetite today."
"Very funny, Rocket Girl," Detective Smith said.
"I didn't eat all the food."
"Well, who did?" Roxy asked.
"Do you have any information about the thief?"
Detective Smith glanced at his notebook.
"I interviewed two workers at Shopwell Supermarket who said the thief is a large—"
[i@Crash!@i] The front of the bakery exploded.
As the dust settled, a large figure stepped out and Roxy gasped.
"A large pig!"
"I'm still hungry," the pig complained, patting his belly.
"It's a talking pig," Roxy whispered to Detective Smith.
"He's holding a rake," Detective Smith said.
The bakery's owner raced outside, yelling, "You destroyed my bakery!"
"Bah!" The pig walked away.
"Stop right there!" Roxy ordered.
The pig snorted. "No!"
[i@Whiz-hoo!@i] Roxy fired her eye laser beams, striking the pig in the face.
"Ouch! How did you do that?" he asked, rubbing his face.
"I have super powers!" Roxy flew into him, and they tumbled across the sidewalk.
People leaped out of the way.
The pig jumped to his feet and swung his rake. "Who are you?"
"Every villain knows who I am," Roxy said, dodging the rake.
[i@Whiz-hoo!@i] She shot her eye laser beams again.
The pig blocked the laser beams with his rake.
"But I'm not a villain—I'm Zhu Bajie."
"Well, I'm Rocket Girl—a powerful superhero!" Roxy said, charging toward Bajie.
Bajie puffed out his chest.
"I'm a powerful spirit!"
He held up his rake, ready to strike, but Roxy slammed into him—[i@pow!@i]
Bajie flew backward.
"Watch out!" A woman on a bike swerved.
[i@Crack!@i] Bajie hit a fire hydrant.
Water sprayed, and a taxi slid into a flower stand.
As Roxy checked on the taxi driver, Bajie rubbed his head.
"I'd better escape," he thought.
"This person is powerful, like a goddess."
Bajie recited a spell.
As he leaped onto a cloud, a delicious aroma drifted through the air toward him.
"What wonderful food is that?" he murmured.
Bajie followed the smell.
It was coming from a building in the distance.
"Where did Zhu Bajie go?" Roxy murmured, looking around.
"The pig flew away on a cloud," Detective Smith said, hurrying over.
Roxy's eyes went wide.
"He can fly? Which way did he go?"
"That way," Detective Smith said, pointing toward Metro City Elementary School.
Roxy flew fast and spotted Bajie landing near the school's entrance.
She landed in front of him.
Bajie waved his rake back and forth. "Leave me alone!"
Roxy grabbed the rake.
"Look!" Mara said. "It's Rocket Girl—she's fighting a pig!"
Roxy's friends ran to the window.
"Let go of my rake!" Bajie shouted.
"No!" Roxy yanked the rake from his hand.
"Go, Rocket Girl," Terrell cried, pumping his fist.
Bajie stomped toward Roxy, but abruptly he stopped to bend over and take a breath.
Roxy scratched her head. "Er . . . What are you doing?"
"Resting," Bajie answered.
Roxy's mouth dropped open. "What?"
"I'm tired!" Bajie yelled, "and I—[i@burp!@i]—I ate too much."
"You're under arrest, Bajie," Roxy said.
Suddenly Bajie pulled a sign out of the ground and flung it at Roxy.
She ducked, and the sign hit a passing truck.
"Ahh!" The driver crashed into a bush.
Roxy hurried away to check on the driver.
When she returned, Bajie had disappeared.
Using her super hearing, she heard snoring.
She followed the sound to the school's equipment shed.
She threw the door open and saw Bajie inside, sleeping on a gym mat.
Slowly and quietly, Roxy lifted Bajie up and carried him off to jail.
Sun Wukong and his companions woke up in a meadow.
Bees buzzed and birds sang as leaves rustled in a gentle breeze.
"What a lovely day," the Tang Monk said.
"Just wait until you see the Western Paradise, Master," Wukong said.
"The weather is always beautiful there."
"I can't wait, so let's start walking," the monk said.
"I'll prepare the horse," Wujing said.
Bajie lay asleep, drooling with his mouth open.
Wukong shook Bajie. "Wake up!"
Bajie rolled over.
"Get up, lazy!" Wukong kicked Bajie.
"Ouch!" Bajie cried, jumping up.
"Why did you do that?"
"You didn't get up," Wukong said.
"You didn't ask politely," Bajie said.
"Yes, I did," Wukong said.
"No, you didn't!" Bajie said.
Just then his stomach growled.
"I'll cook some food for breakfast."
"We'll eat later, Bajie," the Tang Monk said.
"I want to start walking."
"Ugh," Bajie complained. "All we ever do is walk!"
They soon arrived in a mountain village.
"Be careful—demons could be nearby," Wukong warned the others.
"They might want to eat the Tang Monk."
As villagers smiled and waved, Wukong pulled out his iron bar.
The Tang Monk glared at him. "Put that away, Wukong."
"Master is right—this place seems safe," Sha Wujing said.
Wukong sighed and put the bar away.
"Greetings, travelers," a villager said.
"Please come inside and have some breakfast."
"That sounds wonderful!" Bajie said with a grin.
The Tang Monk bowed. "Thank you very much, but we're in a hurry."
Bajie frowned, but Wukong felt relieved.
"I'm glad Master wants to keep walking," he thought.
"This place seems dangerous."
A dark cloud formed in the sky.
"It looks like it will rain," the Tang Monk said, looking up.
"Maybe we should stop here for breakfast."
"That might be a demon," Wukong thought, gazing at the ominous cloud.
He turned to his companions.
"You wait here while I get a look at that cloud.
Don't enter any of these houses until I return."
"Wukong is too careful sometimes," Bajie said with a snort as Wukong flew off.
Just then the Tang Monk felt a raindrop on top of his head.
More drops fell, and suddenly rain poured down, soaking the Tang Monk, Bajie, and Wujing.
A villager opened his door.
"Please come inside where it's warm and dry."
"Yes, let's get out of this rain," the Tang Monk said.
He and his companions hurried into the villager's house.
Up in the sky, Wukong approached the dark cloud.
Hiding behind a smaller cloud, he peeked out at the dark one.
A huge demon sat on it as several small demons bowed to him.
"I knew there was a demon!" Wukong thought.
"Our master, the Demon of Black Rain, is amazing," one small demon said.
"He can make rain!" another one said.
"Yes, I can," the huge demon said with a laugh.
"Soon we'll eat the Tang Monk and live forever!"
The demons laughed and cheered.
"Those demons are dumb—rain won't hurt Master," Wukong murmured, shaking his head.
He went back down to the ground.
When he got there, he gasped in alarm.
"The village is gone!"
The Tang Monk was crying quietly.
"Wukong was right to warn us.
Those nice villagers turned out to be demons!"
Strong ropes tied him to a column.
Bajie and Wujing were tied up too.
"We should have listened to Wukong," Wujing said, struggling to break free.
Bajie twisted in his ropes and shouted, "Villains! Evil demons!
How dare you kidnap us! You'll regret it!
Our good friend, Sun Wukong, will find us!
He's really powerful—even the Jade Emperor is afraid of him!"
Just then his stomach growled.
The Tang Monk frowned.
"Bajie, how can you think about food right now?"
Wujing shook his head. "That's terrible, Bajie."
"I can't help it," Bajie said, continuing to struggle with his ropes.
"I haven't eaten anything today."
The Tang Monk watched Bajie and Wujing squirm wildly.
"Do you think you can break free?"
Bajie grunted. "My ropes are getting loose."
Bajie's yells echoed through the cave.
Several small demons in the kitchen heard him and ran into the throne room.
The Demon of Black Rain glared at them.
"What are you doing? I'm starving!
Why aren't you getting ready to cook the Tang Monk?"
One small demon held up a bowl of spices.
"We are getting ready to cook him, Master!
But the prisoners know Sun Wukong, the Monkey King!"
The Demon of Black Rain yawned.
"Yes, I heard that noisy pig shouting."
"What will we do?" the small demon asked.
"Sun Wukong is powerful. He once defeated Heaven's entire army!"
"Even the Jade Emperor is afraid of him!
If we eat the Tang Monk, Sun Wukong will attack us," another demon said.
A third demon shuddered. "Maybe we shouldn't eat the Tang Monk!"
The Demon of Black Rain held up a hand.
"We will eat the Tang Monk and live forever.
I'm not afraid of Sun Wukong.
Swift Wing knows someone who can help."
A bird demon gasped. "I do?"
The Demon of Black Rain nodded.
"You told me you saw a goddess who was more powerful than Sun Wukong."
A small demon gasped, and he dropped the bowl of spices.
"More powerful than Sun Wukong?"
The small demons looked eagerly at Swift Wing.
"Where is this goddess, Swift Wing?" the Demon of Black Rain asked.
"I'd like to meet her."
"Um, you can't," Swift Wing said. "She's in another world."
The Demon of Black Rain stood up.
"You must know how to get there. Tell me how!"
Shaking, Swift Wing quickly recited a spell.
Light sparkled and then—[i@zoomp!@i] An image appeared.
The image showed a strange kingdom with tall buildings.
"That's where the goddess is," Swift Wing muttered.
"Amazing," the Demon of Black Rain whispered. "The image looks so real."
"It is real," Swift Wing said with a sigh.
"The spell opens a portal to that world.
You can simply step through, and you'll be there."
[i@Crash!@i] A door exploded, and Bajie ran into the throne room.
"I won't let you harm my—Whoa!"
Bajie tripped on the bowl and stumbled through the portal, which closed behind him. [i@Zoomp!@i]
"Why did you eat all that food?" Roxy asked.
Bajie was sitting in a jail cell while Roxy and Detective Smith asked questions.
"I was hungry." Bajie shrugged and looked around.
"Where am I anyway?"
Detective Smith folded his arms. "In jail."
Bajie chuckled. "Oh, I know this is a jail. I've been in jail plenty of times.
In fact, I could easily break out of here if I wanted to.
But I promised the bodhisattva that I'd be good.
It definitely isn't good to break out of jail."
Roxy looked at Detective Smith. "Who's the bodhisattva?"
The detective was writing everything in his notebook. "I have no idea."
"I'm wondering what kingdom I'm in," Bajie went on.
"This place doesn't look like any other kingdom I've seen—the buildings are so tall."
"Metro City isn't a kingdom," Roxy said.
"I guess you've never been here before?"
Bajie shook his head.
"I've been traveling to the West with some friends for a long time.
But this morning some demons kidnapped us."
Detective Smith raised an eyebrow. "You were kidnapped by demons?"
"It happens all the time." Bajie shrugged.
"It's usually not a big deal.
I attacked them and fought very bravely, so they were definitely afraid of me.
But somebody tripped me.
Then all of a sudden, I was here in this kingdom!"
Wukong looked around the mountain where he'd left his companions.
"That village was an illusion," he thought.
"When the Demon of Black Rain made the rainstorm, Master probably entered a house."
Wukong understood why the Tang Monk had fallen for the trick.
But Wujing and Bajie should have known better.
Wukong sighed. "There must be a cave nearby since demons usually live in caves."
Wukong searched all over the mountain's slopes.
Finally he found a door in the side of the mountain.
He pounded on the door and shouted, "Demons! Release my master right now or else!"
Wukong shook his fist and yelled all sorts of terrible things.
Finally the door flew open, and the Demon of Black Rain stomped outside. "You're rude!"
"I'm powerful too!"
Wukong swung his iron bar. [i@Poof!@i]
The demon disappeared, and in his place was a puddle of rainwater.
"Ha!" Wukong smiled. "I destroyed him with one strike!"
He ran into the cave, swinging his iron bar.
"Ahh!" All the small demons screamed and ran out of the cave.
Wukong found the Tang Monk and Wujing, and untied them.
"Thank you, Wukong!" the Tang Monk said.
"You're welcome, Master." Wukong looked around. "Where's Bajie?"
Wujing seemed surprised.
"You didn't see him? He broke free and went to fight the demons."
"He's not in the cave," Wukong said.
The Tang Monk shook his head.
"He kept complaining about being hungry, so he probably went to find food."
Wujing frowned. "And he left us tied up. How terrible!"
Wukong shook his head. "Bajie is awful sometimes."
Just then Wukong heard footsteps and realized a bird demon was trying to sneak by.
Wukong quickly jumped in front of her.
The bird demon stepped back. "Please don't hurt me! I know where your friend is!"
The Demon of Black Rain sat on a cliff, holding his head in his hands.
He stared down.
"Hello, Demon of Black Rain," a fiend said, walking up the cliff.
"What's wrong?"
The demon sighed. "I was preparing a nice dinner when Sun Wukong suddenly attacked me.
I had to flee from my mountain!"
The fiend shook his head.
"Why would you let Sun Wukong bully you like that?"
The demon looked up in surprise. "Sun Wukong is really powerful!"
"Bah!" The fiend waved his hand.
"You shouldn't have to flee from your own mountain."
The demon nodded.
"I wouldn't let Sun Wukong bully [i@me@i]," the fiend said.
The demon made a fist. "Me neither!"
"Where is our friend?" Wukong glared at Swift Wing.
He raised his iron bar.
Swift Wing looked frightened. "He's in another world!"
Wukong lowered his bar. "Another world?"
"How did he get there?" the Tang Monk asked.
"I opened a portal," Swift Wing said.
"Your friend tried to fight the Demon of Black Rain.
But he tripped and fell through the portal."
"I'm confused," Wukong said.
"Why did you open a portal to another world?"
"The Demon of Black Rain made me do it," Swift Wing said.
"A powerful goddess lives in the other world, and the demon wants her help."
"How can she help him?" the Tang Monk asked.
Swift Wing looked down. "She could, um, defeat Wukong."
"What?" Wukong cried, making a fist.
"Nobody can defeat me! If I ever meet that goddess, I'll destroy her!"
"Don't worry about the goddess, Wukong," the Tang Monk said.
"We must find Bajie."
"You're right." Wukong looked at Swift Wing.
"Tell me how to open that portal."
Swift Wing explained the spell to Wukong.
As soon as she was done, Wukong raised his iron bar, and Swift Wing backed away.
"Wukong, what are you doing?" the Tang Monk said.
"She helped us."
"She's a demon, Master, so I have to destroy her," Wukong said.
"I'm sorry," Swift Wing said.
"I used to be a regular bird, but then the demon captured me.
He turned me evil!"
Wukong sighed and lowered his iron bar.
"If you really want to be good again, go to Mount Potalaka."
"To the bodhisattva Guanyin?" Swift Wing asked.
Wukong nodded. "Become Guanyin's student, and she will teach you to be good."
Swift Wing bowed. "I will do that."
The bird demon flapped her wings and flew off.
Wukong recited the spell, and the portal opened, revealing a city filled with tall buildings.
The Tang Monk's eyes went wide. "Wow!"
"You two wait here," Wukong said.
"I'll find Bajie as quickly as I can. Then we'll continue our journey."
Wukong jumped through the portal, which closed behind him.
The Tang Monk sat down.
"You look tired, Master," Wujing said.
"Take a nap while I go outside and check on the horse."
The Tang Monk closed his eyes but soon heard footsteps.
"Are you back already, Wujing?" He opened his eyes—and screamed.
The Demon of Black Rain grinned. "Hello again, Tang Monk!"
Early that evening, Roxy and her friends went to Jack's backyard to play catch.
"Seeing Rocket Girl this morning was so exciting," Terrell said.
As he threw the ball to Roxy, he flashed a quick smile.
"I wonder who that big pig was," Jack said.
"He's obviously an evil villain—he was attacking Rocket Girl," Terrell said.
Roxy threw the ball to Mara.
"In my opinion he's not exactly evil."
Jack raised an eyebrow.
"How would you know, Roxy? You weren't even there."
"Uh-oh," Roxy thought.
"I told Roxy all about the pig," Terrell said quickly.
"But he still seems like a villain to me."
"Whew, saved by Terrell!" Roxy thought in relief.
"Well, I think the pig is funny!" Mara said with a grin.
Roxy's watch beeped. "I'll be right back—I have to call my mom," she said.
Roxy hurried into Jack's front yard and opened her watch.
Mayor Bloom looked upset.
"What's wrong now?" Roxy asked.
"We need help, Rocket Girl," the mayor said.
"A monkey is destroying downtown Metro City!"
"Don't worry, Mayor," Roxy said. "I'm on my way."
Roxy returned to Jack's backyard.
"Hey, guys," she said, "I'll be back soon.
I have to run home for something."
As Roxy started to leave, Terrell hurried after her.
"What's going on—is there a problem in Metro City?"
"Sorry, Terrell, I can't tell you right now. I have to hurry." Roxy ran off.
"Maybe I could have helped," Terrell mumbled as he kicked a pebble.
Then he let out a frustrated sigh. "I wish I had super powers."
When Roxy arrived downtown, she saw people running in every direction.
"That monkey is crazy!"
"Run for your lives!"
"Rocket Girl," a man cried, "you're here—what a relief!"
"Where's the monkey?" Roxy asked.
"He's standing in the intersection," the man said, pointing.
"He keeps yelling at cars and attacking them.
He thinks everyone is trying to hit him."
"Why does he think that?" Roxy asked.
"I have no idea," the man replied with a shrug.
Roxy flew to the intersection.
Smoke filled the air, and smashed cars lined the streets.
She spotted Detective Smith crouching behind a police car.
"Hey, Detective," Roxy said, "you really shouldn't let your pet monkey destroy stuff like that."
"Ha-ha, Rocket Girl." The detective frowned.
"It's not a pet monkey who's doing all the destruction.
It's a talking monkey, kind of like that pig, Bajie."
[i@Smash!@i] [i@Crash!@i] A car flew through the air.
"Oh no!" Roxy flew fast and caught the car.
As she put it down on the street, another car went tumbling through the air.
Roxy gasped. The driver was still inside!
[i@Bang!@i] The car hit the side of the building and fell toward the concrete sidewalk.
"Help, Rocket Girl!" the driver yelled.
Roxy caught the car just before it reached the ground.
She put it down carefully.
The driver stepped out and wiped his forehead.
"Thanks, Rocket Girl!"
Just then a large bus zoomed around a corner and into the intersection.
The monkey raised the iron bar and faced the bus.
"Stop trying to attack me!"
The bus driver saw the monkey and slammed on the brakes.
"Whoa!" he cried as the bus skidded.
[i@Crunch!@i] The monkey struck the bus with his iron bar.
The bus crashed into several trash cans, and the monkey stomped toward it.
Passengers screamed as they scrambled off the bus. "Beware of the monkey!"
"Run for your lives!"
[i@Bam!@i] [i@Crunch!@i] The monkey struck the bus over and over again.
"Stop right there!" Roxy flew toward the monkey, who spun around and hit her with the bar. [i@Wham!@i]
"Ouch!" Roxy cried, rubbing her arm.
The monkey's mouth dropped open in surprise. "My iron bar didn't destroy you!"
"Of course it didn't!" Roxy said, annoyed.
"Grr!" The monkey growled and swung the bar again and again.
Each time Roxy managed to block it with her arm.
Finally the monkey stopped.
"I don't understand what's happening—my iron bar is a treasure from Heaven.
It usually destroys demons."
"I'm not a demon—I'm Rocket Girl," Roxy said.
The monkey twirled the bar in the air.
"Well, I'm Sun Wukong, king of the Fruit and Flower Mountain.
I once defeated Heaven's entire army."
Roxy raised an eyebrow, confused. "Huh?"
Wukong didn't reply as he swung his iron bar again.
[i@Whiz-hoo!@i] Roxy fired her eye laser beams.
They bounced off the bar and hit a mailbox. [i@Boom!@i]
"Oops!" Roxy said.
As Wukong leaped toward Roxy, she jumped out of the way. [i@Whiz-hoo!@i]
She struck Wukong's foot with her eye laser beams.
"Yikes!" Wukong hopped on his other foot.
"What are you doing in Metro City anyway?" Roxy asked.
"I'm looking for my friend," Wukong said, swinging his iron bar.
[i@Bam!@i] A big streetlight crashed into Wukong.
"Got you!" Roxy said, brushing dust off her hands.
Wukong rubbed his head.
He saw a smashed delivery van.
A big grin spread across his face as he picked it up and hurled it at Roxy.
"Oof!" Roxy barely caught it.
"See how strong I am?" Wukong boasted.
"Big deal!" Roxy said as she put the van down.
"I'm super strong too!" Roxy picked up the smashed bus.
With a grunt, she threw it at Wukong.
The bus landed on Wukong.
"Got you again!" Roxy cried.
Suddenly the bus began to rise. Wukong tossed it aside and shrugged.
"So we're both strong, but you should still surrender now.
I have powers that you wouldn't believe."
"Oh yeah?" Roxy took a deep breath. [i@Whoo-oo-oosh!@i]
Her superbreath rushed toward Wukong.
The monkey tumbled backward and slammed into a building.
Wukong stood up and dusted himself off.
Laughing, he walked back to Roxy.
"Until now, I thought you were just some silly little demon.
Now I realize I'm going to need some of my super powers."
"Go ahead and try that, Monkey," Roxy said with a shrug.
"I don't think anyone has more super powers than I do.
In fact, I'm probably the most powerful person in the world!"
Wukong gasped. "It—it's you!"
Roxy frowned. "What are you talking about?"
"You're the goddess Swift Wing told me about."
Wukong said, his eyes blazing with anger.
"She said you were going to help the Demon of Black Rain destroy me!"
"Who are Swift Wing and the Demon of Black Rain?" Roxy thought.
And where had this crazy monkey come from?
Roxy saw Wukong mutter something to himself.
Then she gasped as Wukong began growing tall—really tall!
He soon towered above the city buildings.
Roxy gulped. "How can you . . . ?"
The giant Wukong grabbed her and held her up in front of his face.
"Oh, I guess I didn't tell you," he said with a smile.
"I can grow to any size I want!"
Wukong threw Roxy up in the air.
"So long, Rocket Girl!" He swung his iron bar. [i@Pow!@i]
Tumbling and spinning, Roxy soared into the sky.
"Whoa! I can't stop!" Roxy said as she shot up past the clouds and kept going.
The sky grew darker and darker until Roxy was above Earth's atmosphere.
"I'm in outer space!" Roxy cried.
Finally she slowed down and started falling back toward Earth.
Roxy fell faster and faster. [i@Boomf!@i]
She landed in a deep snowdrift in the mountains.
"Wow," Roxy thought. "Wukong is incredibly powerful!"
"Rocket Girl!" a voice called. "Are you okay?"
A park ranger hurried over and pulled Roxy out of the snowdrift.
"Thanks," Roxy said. "I'm okay . . . I'm trying to fight—"
The park ranger gasped and pointed. "A really big monkey!"
Roxy spun around and saw the giant Wukong flying down toward her.
His iron bar was held high, ready to strike!
"Get out of the way!" Roxy warned the ranger.
The ranger ran as Roxy flew at Wukong. [i@Pow!@i]
Roxy hit the monkey hard.
He fell backward, and the mountain shook.
An avalanche of snow rushed downward.
"Ahh!" The ranger screamed.
Roxy flew fast to grab the ranger and move her out of the way.
When Roxy saw Wukong again, he was his regular size.
"What is he doing now?" Roxy thought.
The strange monkey yanked out a few of his own hairs and blew on them.
Wukong grinned. "This spell is called Body Beyond the Body!"
Roxy screamed as a whole bunch of tiny Wukongs attacked her.
"Grr!" Roxy punched and kicked, sending the Wukongs flying in all directions.
But more kept attacking her.
[i@Whiz-hoo!@i] Her eye laser beams zapped several tiny Wukongs.
[i@Whoo-oo-oosh!@i] Her super breath blew more away, but others kept coming!
Roxy groaned. "This is bad—how will I defeat Wukong?" she thought.
Wukong groaned. "This is bad," he thought.
"The goddess definitely can't destroy me, but I can't destroy her either.
How will I get rid of her?"
He tapped his chin, contemplating the problem. "I know!"
Wukong quietly recited a spell and then called out to the tiny Wukongs. "Return to me!"
All the tiny Wukongs hurried back to Wukong.
"Ha! You're all afraid of me," Roxy cried, shooting after the tiny Wukongs.
